recognize_zh: 周邊血中幾顆小型淋巴球，核染色質濃密並有細溝狀摺痕，右上方細胞核呈摺疊狀，胞質極少，符合小型 Sézary 細胞；此倍率下腦回狀（cerebriform）核只能部分辨識。
features: Small lymphoid cells, near red-cell size, with very high N:C ratio
Dense chromatin with subtle nuclear grooves/folds (best seen in upper cell)
Background red cells with prominent central pallor; no other abnormal cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows scattered small lymphoid cells with very high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, dense chromatin and subtle nuclear grooves and folds, one showing a distinctly convoluted nuclear outline. The cytoplasm is scant and agranular without nucleoli. The cerebriform detail is only partially resolved at this magnification. Findings are compatible with circulating small Sézary cells; diagnosis requires flow cytometry (CD4+ with loss of CD7 and/or CD26, CD4:CD8 ≥10) and a clonal TCR rearrangement matching the skin.

ddx.vs: Normal lymphocytes have smooth round nuclei without grooves; flow loss of CD7/CD26 separates Sézary cells.
CLL cells have round nuclei with coarse 'soccer-ball' chromatin, smudge cells, and CD5+/CD23+ B-cell phenotype.
ATLL cells are larger with multilobated 'flower' nuclei and patients are HTLV-1 positive.
